251108998_c6f17722.text: The reticular thalamic nucleus (RTn) articulates oscillations in large neuronal assemblies (Crick, 1984)(Halassa et al., 2016). GABAergic neurons in the RTn receive collaterals from thalamocortical (TC) and corticothalamic (CT) fibers and these connections modulate information transfer between thalamic nuclei and the cerebral cortex (Guillery et al., 2003)(Pinault, 2004). The RTn also receives inputs from noradrenergic, serotonergic, and cholinergic clusters in the brainstem (Asanuma, 1992)(Ben-Ari et al., 1976) (Cropper et al., 1984)(Hallanger et al., 1987)(Paré et al., 1988). These afferents control electrophysiological properties and regulate all TC activity. In this way, the RTn in combination with its afferents induces oscillations associated with functions such as attention, sleep, and consciousness (Clemente-Perez et al., 2017)(Crick, 1984)(Steriade, 2005)

251108998_6032faf3.text: .The topographic organization of projections results in the formation of functional sectors in the RTn: one limbic sector, five sensory sectors, and one motor sector (Crabtree, 1992)(Lam et al., 2011). In rodents, the motor sector is in the rostral region of the RTn (Gonzalo-Ruiz et al., 1995)(Pinault et al., 1998)(Pinault, 2004) and receives GABAergic projections from the globus pallidus (GP; external GP in primates) (Asanuma et al., 1990)(Cornwall et al., 2004)(Gandia et al., 1993)(Hazrati et al., 1991)(Kayahara et al., 1998).
